text: Ahmed Ashour says his family left Jaffa in 1948 expecting to return the next day; Adin asks what they expected to happen before that return. They expected the Jews to be killed so they could return. This is the fake Nakba they claim. If they were truly ejected by Israel, there would be no reason for them to hope "to return the next day." They expected the Arabs to completely wipe out the Jews.

An Arab pilot stabbed his co-pilot and attempted to hijak an Israel-bound flydubai flight when Israeli passengers miraculously saved the plane after a nosedive. CNN called it an “altercation,” the New York Times an “altercation between the pilot and co-pilot,” AFP said the pilots “fought,” the WSJ a “struggle,” Sky News a “brawl,” and the BBC a “fight between pilots.” Ben Shapiro: an attempt to murder 180 mostly Israeli passengers by crashing the plane.

NPR says the Palestinian Authority's pay for slay program, which pays families of terrorists who murder or maim Jews, "a controversial program that pays the families of Palestinians who are detained in Israeli jails or killed or injured by the Israeli military."

CNN and TRT report Gaza cemetery destruction in 2024; Aizenberg contrasts that reporting with the January 2026 recovery of Ran Gvili’s remains from a Gaza cemetery, accompanied by IDF footage and photographs.
David Collier challenges the BBC's football-pitch demolition story for omitting the pitch's proximity to Israel's security fence and disputes the legality of its construction.
Aizenberg challenges Reuters’ presentation of Gaza war-crime allegations, pointing to the article’s account that US government lawyers could not make a legal finding.
The BBC interviews the crying sister of Palestinian prisoner Murad Abu al-Rub without mentioning his four life sentences for involvement in a suicide bombing that killed four Israelis.
Richard Tice highlights reporting that a BBC Gaza documentary ignored evidence of Hamas killing Palestinians in humanitarian aid queues, obscuring responsibility for their deaths.

The Independent maps the countries Israel has attacked; HonestReporting supplies the omitted context: Hamas’s October 7 massacre, Iranian proxy warfare, Hezbollah rockets, Houthi missiles and drones, and Qatar’s sheltering of Hamas leaders.

What's insane is Hamas builds 1000s of rockets & tunnels diverting $100mm/year from this effort. Hamas brags about using water pipes for rockets in this Al Jazeera report. Maybe focus on that first to realize why Israel limits good in the first place.

Just checked media coverage of the damning revelations from the Motaz Azaiza interview: CNN site: 0 mentions NBC News: 0 mentions  Reuters: 0 mentions AP: 0 mentions NYT: 0 mentions  Washington Post: 0 mentions. All of these orgs have repeatedly promoted him in the past.
A compilation contrasts an edited accusation against Shabbos Kestenbaum with fuller remarks about prosecuting vandalism of a synagogue.
Kenneth Roth claims 83% of Gaza’s dead were civilians, but Aizenberg points out that that figure is only deaths the IDF can not ID by first and last name. Second Aizenberg post links to his proof.
A Hamas recruitment announcement identifies the struck Ain al-Hilweh site as a training facility, contradicting the group’s denial of military use.
The Mossad challenges Dilly Hussain’s use of a cropped age-of-consent headline and an unrelated Israel-account reply to portray Israel as endorsing child sexual abuse.
A response to “he only threw a rock” recalls four-year-old Adele Biton, who died after a Palestinian rock attack caused the car carrying her to crash.

Political economist Ashok Kumar celebrates released novelist Bassem Khandaqji without mentioning his three life sentences for helping carry out the 2004 Carmel Market bombing: he drove the teenage bomber to Tel Aviv using a journalist ID to pass checkpoints; three Israelis were killed.
Antizionist Richard Medhurst calls Samir Abu Nimeh a Palestinian “hostage” without mentioning his involvement in a bus bombing that killed six Israelis and a grenade attack that killed another.
Censored Humans portrays Mahmoud Issa through his long imprisonment and solitary confinement, omitting his kidnapping and murder of Israeli police officer Nissim Toledano.

A response challenges climate scientist Julia Steinberger’s comparison of Israel’s strike on Hezbollah’s headquarters with the September 11 attacks, pointing to the terrorist command meeting at the target.

Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib says Israel is murdering ceasefire negotiators and has no interest in a deal after the Doha strike. Researcher Mark Zlochin answers the negotiating-team argument with a September 9 report that Hamas rejected the US proposal as a surrender deal.

Journalist Mehdi Hasan calls Israel’s strike on Houthi leaders the wiping out of a Middle Eastern government, while the screenshot’s community note points out that the Houthis are not Yemen’s recognized government and are in fact a terrorist organization.
